newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-ATHLETICS-Top NZ sprinter training in Australia.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-ATHLETICS-Top NZ sprinter training in Australia.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Jan 9 - Top New Zealand sprinter Gus Nketia is training in Australia after refusing to go outside Auckland to find a compatible Kiwi coach, NZPA reports.

Nketia, who will race in the 100m against nine-time Olympic champion Carl Lewis at this month's Robin Tait Classic, is working with Cliff Mallett, one of two track and field coaches at the Queensland Institute of Sport in Brisbane.
The Ghanian-born runner, who sprinted for New Zealand in the 100m at Atlanta, moved to Queensland on the advice of German relay and sprints coach Ralph Mochbahani.
Nketia, a member of the North Shore Bays club, has worked with Mochbahani for the past 18 months; he was previously coached by former Aucklander Kerry Hill.
Athletics New Zealand director of coaching Stephen Hollings said this week: "It seems to be working out fine.
"Gus is running in Canberra this weekend and then coming over and doing the Smokefree (international track series) and the Robin Tait."
He said Nketia was then looking at heading back to Australia to run in some of the grand prix meets and returning to for the New Zealand track and field championships.
Hollings said it was a shame he had had to go to Australia to train. Attempts to find a compatible coach for Nketia in the Auckland region had failed.
"Gus really wasn't prepared to live anywhere else in New Zealand, other than in Auckland."
Hollings said Nketia was not receiving any financial support from Athletics NZ's high performance programme for living in Brisbane, or for travelling there.
"We're only doing for him what we would do with any other athlete of his ability in terms of getting him to meetings," he said.
There were several other athletes who could not be matched to coaches in the areas they lived.
